source.notes: arch-074 (flagship Nest combinator). Masked second-order UNNORMALIZED causal case (paper Eq. 3.3 + Algorithm 1, the default operator). The Nest combinator composes through the public graph as TWO DEPENDENT typed K2 calls — S_t = S_(t-1) + k_t k_tᵀ, r_t = S_t q_t (call 1: query=q,key=k,value=k); F_t = F_(t-1) + r_t v_tᵀ, o_t = q_tᵀ F_t (call 2: query=q,key=r,value=v). Both are the plain additive K2 law (delta=False, gate_scope=none, scale_rule=one, after-update read); the paper's F_t = S_tC_t − G_t expands to exactly the second call's state, and S_t symmetric makes call 1's output orientation exact. The two states (S, F) are explicit producer-carried edges; r is materialized between calls; unfused (two launches). Verified against the pinned paper (HLA.pdf, arXiv 2510.27258, @ 484fef2b). Layer module: architectures/hla.py.

params.combinator: Nest: two dependent additive K2 calls (S_t state, then F_t state) composed via producer/consumer edges — the exact factorization of the masked unnormalized law
external_stages: none for the mixer (executes through public K2); q/k/v construction is upstream of the layer
params.note: default masked unnormalized causal case only; unfused two-K2 composition

state.state_bundle: (S, F) — one additive K2 state per call, both carried for continuation

coverage.notes: The public two-K2 Nest graph matches the independent serial Algorithm 1 recurrence (hla_serial_reference) AND an independent brute-force transcription of the closed-form masked identity; the strict-causality gate (future-token perturbation does not change earlier outputs); and gradients through the pair — in tests/test_architectures_hla.py. NOT claimed (sweep verdict): the normalized variant (Eq. 3.4, +ε), decay γ (Eq. 4.1), ridge λ, the chunk-parallel associative scan, and the fused single-kernel schedule (the two-K2 composition is unfused; fusion is a later proven rewrite).
